name: cpp-httplib
baseline: C++ REST SDK (cpprestsdk) v2.10.15 HTTP server
workload: Independent shootout: 10 Python producer processes each POST 1000 small JSON messages to a /test echo endpoint with 0 ms handling time on the same machine, 28 service threads; metric is wall time from first request to last reply.
claimed_speedup: Local, N=1000, t=0 ms, C=28: cpp-httplib v0.5.8 3.015 s vs C++ REST SDK 3.401 s (about 1.13x faster, derived from page data; numbers read from images/rest_all.PNG). With 4 service threads the C++ REST SDK deadlocked and cpp-httplib finished in 1.915 s. In the same table cpp-httplib is slower than Crow (1.536 s), Pistache (1.059 s), Restbed (1.333 s) and Restinio (1.025 s).
compiler_and_flags: CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 14, thread pool left at the library default (CPPHTTPLIB_THREAD_POOL_COUNT define commented out in basic-httplib/main.cpp); compiler and version not stated
hardware: 28x Intel Xeon CPU E5-2660 v4 @ 2.0 GHz, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu 16.04.3 LTS
tradeoffs: Single-header, blocking socket I/O with a thread pool only; HTTP/1.1 only (no HTTP/2 or HTTP/3); 32-bit platforms not supported. Easiest integration of the six frameworks compared, but no event loop, so many idle connections cost threads.
caveats: Weak and mixed evidence. cpp-httplib's authors make no speed claim; the repo has a benchmark/ directory that builds a Crow v1.3.1 server beside cpp-httplib (Makefile bench-all) but publishes no numbers. The only numbers found are third-party and from 2020 (cpp-httplib v0.5.8, C++ REST SDK v2.10.15, both much older than the current release v0.60.0). The 1.13x win over C++ REST SDK holds in one table cell only: at N=1000, t=0 ms over VPN with C=28 cpp-httplib took 3:31.510 against 1:52.476, and in the t=200 ms cells it ties or trails (3:21.790 against 3:21.415 local C=28; 14:31.857 against deadlock over VPN C=4). It is slower than Crow, Pistache, Restbed and Restinio in the sprint cell, and the shootout README's wording that Httplib 'followed' Restinio in the sprint cases does not match its own table. The harness is client-bound and noisy: a Python http.client loop opens a new connection per request and prints under a lock, services log through log4cplus, only about 10,000 requests per cell (about 3k req/s), single run per cell with no repeats or variance, C++ REST SDK deadlocks when threads are fewer than producers. Numbers exist only as a table image in the README; the README text states just 'over 3 times faster' for Restinio against C++ REST SDK. Compiler version not stated. Own A/B script benchmark/ab.sh in the repo compares two cpp-httplib refs, not another library. The guessed baseline (OpenSSL) and category (tls) were wrong; the repo is an HTTP server and client library and was refiled under http-servers-frameworks.
found_via: seed-record pass from https://github.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp#Networking; evidence found via microsoft/cpprestsdk issue #1432 'C++ REST frameworks benchmark' which links https://github.com/guteksan/REST-CPP-benchmark
